answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprint Rule. Each identity stores a hash of its interaction graph per epoch; continuity requires new-epoch behaviour to overlap the prior fingerprint above a fixed threshold. Sudden resets flag a reef of stale clones, forcing attackers to maintain each fake identity across many epochs. Genuine agents drift slowly, like an oasis persisting through drought. A raven account that vanishes and returns cannot re-enter without replaying full history. Attacker cost: sustained compute and coordination for every identity, every epoch, with no cheap reset.
